incident-bot: PROD ALERT: p99 streaming decode latency > 2.0s across prod-west (cluster: infer-west-2). Threshold breached at 2025-06-12 21:03:19 UTC :rotating_light:

amelia: seeing p95 ~ 650ms, p99 spikes up to 2.4s. streaming sessions dropping. Noticed spike started ~ 21:00 UTC after the TRT8 runtime push.

raja: confirmed, we rolled TRT8 + flashattn kernels at 20:45 for model:gpt-medium-8b-v2. Metrics show a step increase in tail latency correlated with kernel build 2025-06-12T20:43:00Z (build-id abc1234). Quick logs from the hosts: 
```
2025-06-12T21:00:58Z decode: tail latency 2450ms kernel=trt8-flashattn-abc1234
2025-06-12T21:01:02Z kv-evict: pagefault hit
```

lucas: paging events spiking on the same hosts, looks like compilepath filler causing extra device memory churn. Also seeing more CUDA memcopies during decode loops.

tina: CS reporting 3 customers hitting degraded streaming experiences, two of them on Dedicated pools (tenant-id: T-72, T-301).

amelia: mitigation plan: 1) route traffic to fallback model-variant (gpt-medium-8b-v1-quant) 2) disable flashattn kernel flag on runtime nodes 3) scale dedicated pools for affected tenants.

raja: starting immediate rollback for the kernel on canary cohort and enabling runtime flag `--disable-flashattn` for runtime nodes in prod-west. Commands I'm running now:
```
./infra/rollforward.sh --target canary --build-id abc1234 --action revert
redwood-runtime --set-flag disable_flashattn=true --env prod-west
```
deploy-bot: Rollback job queued: job-id 7890, eta ~90s

amelia: routing rule updated: traffic split 60/40 fallback->new. Watch p99.

lucas: quick probe: ran `dmesg` and `nvprof` on one host, saw kernel compilepath allocations spike during decode; suspect new libcudnn scheduling causing small page faults and extra host-device memcpy.

raja: applying a runtime config patch on canary to force continuous-batching fallback and to tighten kv-cache retention:
```
# runtime config snippet
batcher.allow_shadow_padding=false\nbatcher.force_kv_cache=true\nkv_cache.eviction_threshold=0.85\n
```

jess: alerted infra to hold any new TRT builds from auto-promote until we finish forensics. Put a temporary gate on the pipeline.

amelia: p99 back down to 920ms on canary after rollback and config patch. prod-west overall p99 at 1.1s and trending down.

tina: contacting CS customers now to confirm mitigation; relaying ETA for resolution ~ 30-45 min and that dedicated pools were scaled for short-term capacity.

lucas: preliminary root-cause hypothesis: TRT8 flashattn kernel combined with a new compiler flag set in abc1234 (`-fno-fast-math` toggled) triggered an alternate code path that increases pagewalks in the KV/cache access pattern under high concurrency. Need to reproduce with long sequences (seq_len >= 1024).

raja: I'll open a repro job and a PR containing a stress script targeting seq_len=2048, qps=1k, concurrent streams=200 to compare abc1229 (last known-good) vs abc1234. Will attach perf traces.

amelia: handoff to night oncall @lucas in 30m. Leaving the current mitigation state in notes.

amelia: RUNBOOK (short):
- check p95/p99 in dashboards (dash: infra/streaming/p99)
- confirm rollback job 7890 completed on canary and stopped promote
- verify `disable_flashattn` flag present on prod-west runtime nodes
- confirm dedicated pools scaled for tenants T-72,T-301
- collect `perf record -g` traces and dmesg from affected hosts
- stash nvprof / nvtx traces to s3://redwood-forensics/abc1234/
- if p99 > 1.5s for 15m escalate to SRE lead (pager)

lucas: ack, I'll pick up the runbook and continue triage. I'll keep the rollback in place for canary and slowly expand to prod if we can validate.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: status=mitigating, impacted=3 tenants, user-visible=partial, started=1768009999, update_ts=1768013432

amelia: thanks team — I'll kick off a postmortem doc after we validate root cause. Adding notes to the incident board.

lucas: quick note for followup: reproduce needed on an isolated infra stack with identical GPU drivers + TRT8 build. Also check the compiler toolchain patch in CI that introduced the flag.

amelia: handing over. lucas, escalate to runtime-lead if we hit sustained p99 > 1.2s for 20m.

lucas: will do. signing off for the handoff window -> monitoring.
